newsitem.title: CANADA: Wharf likes new Goldcorp bid.
newsitem.headline: Wharf likes new Goldcorp bid.

text.p: Goldcorp Inc's C$86 million bid for the 49.7 percent of Wharf Resources Ltd it does not own looks better than a previous failed bid, said the chairman of an independent committee formed to evaluate the bid.
"The last one was a bust. This one is different," Mike McMurrich, also an independent director of Wharf, said in an interview.
The cash or share bid would give Wharf shareholders more liquidity, and the larger merged company would likely put a premium on the shares, McMurrich said.

Goldcorp made an all-stock bid last December but withdrew its offer in February after the independent committee asked for more, Goldcorp and Wharf president Robert McEwen said in a telephone interview.
The problem with the last bid was that the Goldcorp share price was very volatile, making it difficult to nail down the value of the offer, said McMurrich.

The bid presented by Goldcorp on Wednesday offered C$9 cash or 0.72 of a class A subordinated voting share of Goldcorp for each common share of Wharf. The cash option put a floor value on the offer, McMurrich said.
Goldcorp also said Wednesday it entered into a bought deal with Gordon Capital and Griffiths McBurney and Partners to issue 3.2 million shares at C$12.50 per share.
The share issue made it easier for Wharf to evaluate Goldcorp shares, McMurrich said.

The independent committee has started looking for legal and financial advisers to evaluate the offer. The committee expected to send its recommendation to shareholders before November 11, McMurrich said.
The merger should be competed by the end of the year, McEwen said.
Wharf's main asset, the Wharf mine in South Dakota, produces about 95,000 ounces of gold a year. It also has the rights to potential gold resources on neighboring properties.

Goldcorp had consolidated gold production of 198,000 ounces in 1995, including all of Wharf's production. Production in 1996 is expected to be lower because of a strike at its Red Lake property in Northern Ontario.
Investors bumped Wharf Resources up 1.30 to 9.20 in trading of more than 739,000 shares by mid-afternoon Wednesday.
McMurrich said he did not expect a competing bid.
